question: origin of generic-bearing symbol names in functions.json 'names'
evidence: workgraph names for each function = union of native-procedures.json[name] (from `llvm-pdbutil dump --symbols`) and public-symbols.json[demangled].
native-procedures.json generator scripts/render-skeleton/inventory.py parses `llvm-pdbutil dump --symbols --modi=N` output; llvm-pdbutil does NOT demangle (its --publics output keeps raw _ZN).

The exact string 'rhapsody::raw::device::GraphicsDevice::queue_submit<alloc::vec::Vec<rhapsody::raw::submit::SubmitInfo,alloc::alloc::Global>,rhapsody::rg::executor::impl$7::submit_pending_cbs::closure_env$0>' exists verbatim as a null-terminated byte string in tiny_glade.pdb at file offset 31700481.

The raw legacy-mangled symbol for queue_submit is _ZN8rhapsody3raw6submit55_$LT$impl$u20$rhapsody..raw..device..GraphicsDevice$GT$12queue_submit17h8a0ca96aebdf4411E -- it carries NO generic arguments. The stored pretty name DOES carry generics, so the name was emitted by the toolchain from typed debug info, not by demangling the mangled name.

llvm-cxxfilt on that mangled symbol yields the poorer 'rhapsody::raw::submit::_$LT$impl$u20$rhapsody..raw..device..GraphicsDevice$GT$::queue_submit::h8a0ca96aebdf4411' (no generics). Thus cxxfilt != stored name.

signature_encoding.S_PUB32/S_GPROC32/S_LPROC32 names: legacy _ZN mangling is the underlying symbol; legacy encodes the def-path AND generic arguments of the item, but NOT the plain parameter/return signature. The stored S_GPROC32 name is a compiler-pretty form = path + concrete generic args + {impl#N}/{closure#N} disambiguators.
signature_encoding.LF_FUNC_ID/LF_MFUNC_ID: store demangled function names referenced by S_*_ID records; do NOT encode signatures.
signature_encoding.S_INLINESITE: references LF_FUNC_ID index of the inlined callee; no signature.

v0_subset.note: only _RTC_Initialize/_RTC_Terminate (MSVC runtime checks); NO Rust v0 (_R<base62>) symbols anywhere. v0 would encode full signature, but none present.

natvis.value: confirms field names/offsets for windows-rs wrapper types only; NOTHING about rhapsody/country-core types.

legacy_hash_cross_build.17h<hash>: stable deterministic hash of legacy def-path+types for a fixed rustc; usable for cross-build matching ONLY if same rustc+same crate structure.
legacy_hash_cross_build.skeleton_A_B_C: skeleton/A|B|C contain only Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock (no src, no compiled symbols, zero 17h hashes); no cross-build matching possible now.

credits_crates.value: credits-crates.txt lists only shipped/attributed crates; symbols from crates in Cargo.lock but not credits (e.g. bindgen, clang-sys, platform shims) are build/platform deps. Symbol ownership by crate is readable directly from the module name (rhapsody-*, country_core-*) rather than credits.

caveats: public-symbols.json['demangled'] is a PROJECT-SIDE llvm-cxxfilt of the raw _ZN name; it is lossy (keeps $LT$/$u20$ escapes, drops generics) and must NOT be used for type claims. 0 of its 101405 entries contain a real generic <...> (all use $LT$).
The stored pretty names encode generic INSTANTIATION (true monomorphizations of THIS binary), not a full Rust signature; parameter/return types absent.
{impl#N}/{closure#N} disambiguators (impl$7, impl$11, closure_env$0) are build/source-specific and meaningless without source.
